plain_summary: For an adult outpatient with established CKD, review the dose of sitagliptin, saxagliptin, alogliptin or vildagliptin against its own Australian renal dosing bands.

medicine_groups.name: Gliptins with medicine-specific renal dose limits
medicine_groups.note: Check each ingredient independently. For combination tablets use each component strength. Add doses only across products that are actually concurrent. Kidney values must be in the unit stated for that medicine.

needs_facts.meets: CKD was established by the supply date. If timing is unknown and could change the comparison, ask whether CKD had been diagnosed by then. If dialysis could change the decision and there is no applicable stable kidney result, ask whether the person was on dialysis at the time of supply.

options.words: CKD was established by the supply date
CKD was absent at the supply date
CKD is known now but its timing is unclear

needs_facts.meets: Use a dated CrCl in mL/min applicable at supply with stable kidney function. A validated Cockcroft-Gault calculation needs contemporaneous age, sex, weight and serum creatinine in µmol/L with the weight basis recorded. Use this measure for alogliptin only. Ask where the latest kidney test can be checked and obtain the dated result. If a typed result has no date, verify when it applied before confirming an excess.

Use a dated, stable indexed eGFR in mL/min/1.73 m² applicable at supply for sitagliptin, saxagliptin or vildagliptin. Ask whether a kidney blood test has been done and where the dated result can be checked. An undated typed result leaves the comparison open until its timing is checked.

Documented maintenance dialysis at the time of supply sets daily ceilings of 25 mg for sitagliptin, 6.25 mg for alogliptin and 50 mg for vildagliptin, and warrants review of saxagliptin at any dose. Ask whether the person was on dialysis at the time of supply. If dialysis status changed, check dated evidence for each supply under review. If off dialysis, apply the kidney result for that medicine.

rule_for_models: For an adult outpatient with established CKD, use the strength and directions to total the same gliptin in products taken together. Exclude switches and count only the gliptin component. Diabetes type is not required. Use stable indexed eGFR in mL/min/1.73 m² for sitagliptin, saxagliptin and vildagliptin. For sitagliptin, the daily maximum is 100 mg at an indexed eGFR of 45 or higher (including exactly 45), 50 mg from 30 to below 45, and 25 mg below 30 or on dialysis. For saxagliptin, the daily maximum is 5 mg at an indexed eGFR of 45 or higher and 2.5 mg from 15 to below 45, and review any use below 15 or on dialysis. For alogliptin, use creatinine clearance in mL/min with daily ceilings of 25 mg above 50, 12.5 mg from 30 to 50, and 6.25 mg below 30 or on dialysis. For alogliptin on peritoneal dialysis, a daily dose above 6.25 mg remains a confirmed finding, and note in the finding that alogliptin has not been studied in peritoneal dialysis. For vildagliptin, use a daily ceiling of 50 mg at an indexed eGFR below 60 or on dialysis. Apply these dialysis rules whenever maintenance dialysis (haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis) is documented, even without a numeric kidney result. When a dated stable kidney result is recorded and dialysis is not documented, do not treat absent dialysis status as a missing fact. If dialysis status changed, use dated evidence for each supply before confirming a finding. Off dialysis, apply the usual renal bands. Cite the supply and applicable clinical evidence for an excess or an any-use review. Report no finding for an exclusion or a dose within the applicable limit. If missing dose, concurrent use, eligibility, kidney function at supply or dialysis details could change the decision, report only a possible finding and name the gap.
cannot_be_seen: Dispensing does not establish the dose taken. Kidney results obtained elsewhere, their units and their timing may be missing.
ask_the_gp: Could you review the daily dose of the gliptin identified in this finding against the patient's kidney function and dialysis status at the time of supply?
